brief.offer: Managed backup and recovery for small Manila offices. Nightly encrypted backups of servers and workstations to two locations (a Makati data center and offsite cold storage in Clark), quarterly restore drills with a signed report, and a 4-hour recovery time objective for critical files. PHP 18,500 per month for up to 15 machines, no setup fee, cancel with 30 days notice.
brief.audience: Owners and office managers of 10-to-40-person firms in Metro Manila (law offices, accounting firms, clinics) who currently back up to a USB drive in a desk drawer, or to nothing. They have lost files before. They do not know what RPO means and do not want to.
brief.voice: Plain, direct, slightly dry. Talks like a careful engineer, not a salesman. Never scares the reader with doom scenarios; states facts and lets them land. Short sentences.
facts: Founded 2019, run by two former bank infrastructure engineers
Backs up 214 machines across 19 client offices today
Last quarterly restore drill: 100 percent of sampled files recovered, average 41 minutes
Backups are encrypted before they leave the office; Salcedo staff cannot read file contents
imagery: the inside of a small Manila server room at night, two racks, cabling visible, lit only by equipment LEDs and one overhead fluorescent
a quiet law office at dusk after everyone has left, desks with closed laptops, warm lamp light through a window

reflexRejected.secondOrder: a laminated server maintenance log or asset checklist, the document reflex for anything technical and regulated

direction.aestheticLane: photographic, object-anchored, unhurried — two real rooms carry the page instead of icons or stat walls

inverseTest.competitorSentence: A backup-service landing page with a hero stat wall (99.99% uptime, 24/7 monitoring, bank-grade encryption) over a pricing table and three feature cards with lock icons.
inverseTest.whyThisIsNotThat: This page has one photograph of the actual server room, one photograph of an actual client office, one CTA, and one proof fact from a real drill — no icon grid, no invented uptime number, no tiers.

theme.scene: An office manager reads this at 6pm after everyone else has left, laptop closed, in the last warm light before dark, wondering whether tonight's backup will actually run.

hero.headline: Backups that actually restore. Four-hour recovery, in writing.
